text:
elaine: Quick sync  — proposing a "garden-shed" refactor pattern: pull one tiny tenant-facing responsibility out of session-sidecar into a small, replaceable "shed" process. Idea is incremental decoupling with minimal ops burden. Thoughts?

rajar: Nice metaphor. Can you give a concrete example?

elaine: Example: the multi-tenant request-coalescer. The shed would own per-tenant coalescing queues, backoff, and metrics. session-core keeps only cross-tenant orchestration and final routing.

tom: Migration plan? How do we keep correctness during cutover?

elaine: Phases: shadow, sticky-route reads, authoritative reads, then prune. Shadow mode collects metrics but doesn't affect production responses. Sticky-route prefers shed but allows fallback. Authoritative flips the switch. Each phase has gating windows and automated rollback.

rajar: What about consistency and cross-tenant operations?

elaine: Sheds are tenant-local by design. Cross-tenant joins remain in session-core. For rare cases where a shed must consult core, we use a sync fetch API with short timeouts and circuit breakers.

ops-bot: /cohort create shed-cohort-alpha -> id: sc-1745799

tom: Performance: extra hop vs reduced locking?

elaine: Measured hypothesis: cold-path p50 +0.8–1.5ms; p95 improves under load because we remove a global lock and reduce heap churn. We'll validate with 48h shadow replays and targeted tail tests.

rajar: Rollout gates? metrics?

elaine: Gate on p95_latency, error_rate, cache_miss_rate (if applicable), and a small quality eval on end-to-end correctness. Automatic rollback if p95 > +10% absolute or error_rate +1% absolute. Also track shed_memory and shed_queue_depth.

tom: Ops overhead? Too many sheds = config sprawl.

elaine: Sheds run the same binary with flags (mode, mem_budget, queue_limit). We expose three knobs only: mem_budget, concurrency, and log_level. Defaults safe; only big tenants get custom budgets. Single observability model — traces tagged with shed=true and tenant_cohort.

rajar: Tests & canary plan?

elaine: Staging: traffic replay 1x and 3x, chaos test shed disconnects. Prod canary: 0.5% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 24h hold at 25% for higher-risk cohorts. We'll schedule the 5% step during a low-traffic window.

tom: Can you paste the shadow-run snippet?

elaine: Sure:

```
# run shed in shadow mode for tenant T
./bin/shed --tenant $TENANT --mode=shadow --mem-budget=64MB --log-level=info
```

rajar: Who writes the RFC and owns rollout?

elaine: I'll draft a short RFC (motivation, contract, migration plan, gating, cost). @tom to add runbook commands and rollback script, @rajar to run staging replays. I'll own perf analysis.

ops-bot: cohort sc-1745799 created and scheduled for initial shadow-run (start in 2h)

tom: Action items:
- elaine: RFC draft by Tue EOD
- tom: runbook + rollback cmds by Wed
- rajar: staging replay harness + baseline by Thu
- elaine: perf replay results posted in this thread after run

rajar: Add a short cost section in the RFC — projection for steady-state and transient cutover cost.

elaine: Will do. Also propose we track a small "debt-meter" in the epic: number of shared-hotpaths removed and p95 tail delta. Helps quantify payoff.

tom: +1 to debt-meter. Also add sample dashboards to the RFC (p95, error_rate, shed_mem, shed_qdepth).

elaine: Thanks — I'll post the RFC link here when ready and attach the sample dashboards. :seedling:
